description.narrative:
Indicator – Capacity building: public and private sector representatives reached by training on climate, energy, biomethane, and Just Transition At least 100 people participating in project workshops and other project activities increase their awareness of just transition, energy transition, and green recovery (milestone/target: 100).
What was done this quarter: During this quarter, the first workshop under this indicator was conducted, gathering 56 participants representing industrial communities, local authorities, civil society, and experts. This means that slightly more than 50% of the target (100 participants) has already been achieved. The remaining share of the indicator will be reached through the upcoming workshops and activities planned for the next reporting period, in line with the Work Plan. The method used was a Google Form

Target audience: Local authorities’ representatives
Description of the participants:
Total: 56 participants, Sex: Male - 31, Female- 25, Disability: Unknown, Age: Unknown, Geography: Unknown, Actor receiving support: Unknown, Sector: Unknown.

The 1st workshop was on the topic of green reconstruction and preparation of projects in the field of renewable energy, energy efficient and environmental protection. The event was conducted, gathering 56 participants representing industrial communities, local authorities, civil society, and experts. This means that slightly more than 50% of the target (100 participants) has already been achieved. The remaining share of the indicator will be reached through the upcoming workshops and activities planned for the next reporting period, in line with the Work Plan. The method used was a Google Form.
More than three dozen communities from different regions of Ukraine with coal, oil and gas, metallurgical, or other industrial enterprises were identified, including nine new communities: Kryvyi Rih, Nikopol, Zaporizhzhia, Nadvirna, Dolyna, Drohobych, Kremenchuk, Kamianske and Okhtyrka.
The first day focused on analysing community challenges, discussing expectations from participation in the project, and defining key thematic areas for further work. Through panel discussions, facilitated group sessions, and interactive exercises, participants developed a shared understanding of barriers and opportunities and emphasised the important role of civil society organisations in supporting dialogue, citizen engagement, and horizontal exchange of experience.
The second day was practical and aimed at strengthening communities’ capacity to attract funding for recovery and green transformation initiatives. Participants received an overview of available funding sources, donor and state requirements, and project formats that typically receive support. A key outcome of the workshop was the clearly expressed need for continuous communication, exchange of best practices, and community-building, which will be further incorporated into the project’s upcoming activities.
